about: Open tundra and steppe tundra, moving with time: where people walked the cold open ground, and how its edges changed as the ice came and went.
layout: Uint32 cell index x ncell, then nstep x ncell bytes. Byte: bits 1-7 are the tundra weight 0..254, bit 0 is 1 where the source class is Steppe tundra.

sourced.vegetation: Beyer, R.M., Krapp, M. & Manica, A. (2020). High-resolution terrestrial climate, bioclimate and vegetation for the last 120,000 years. Scientific Data 7, 236. doi:10.1038/s41597-020-0552-1; data pastclim_Beyer2020 v1.1.0, Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.7062281, CC BY 4.0. BIOME4 vegetation class at 0.5 degrees, 72 timesteps from 120,000 years ago to the present.
sourced.what_counts: BIOME4 classes 22 Steppe tundra, 23 Shrub tundra, 24 Dwarf shrub tundra, 25 Prostrate shrub tundra, 26 Cushion forb lichen moss tundra.

drawn: A 1.0-cell blur on the class boundaries, and the interpolation between the source’s own timesteps at render time. Nothing else. The vegetation classes are the source’s; this map did not classify a climate field itself.
not_drawn: Nothing before 120,000 years ago, because the reconstruction begins there. The blank is not an absence of tundra; it is an absence of anyone who reconstructed it. Class 28 Land ice is cut from the mask, so tundra is never painted on the source’s own ice; the map’s ice layer is a different reconstruction (NADI-1, DATED-1, PATICE) and the two will not agree at the edges.
rejected: CHELSA-TraCE21k was evaluated first and not used: about 4 TB, and its licence is stated inconsistently across its own records (CC BY 2.0 in the paper, CC BY-SA 4.0 in the EnviDat metadata licence field). This map has already refused CShapes for being ShareAlike.
